title: Orient shelter entrances relative to prevailing wind and storm shifts
observation: Shelter wedge and streamlines replace process boxes. The low-back label crosses airflow and the lee drift note grazes grade. Move the labels and retain the changing-wind limit.

title: Separate conductive, convective, radiative and evaporative heat loss
observation: Four arrows show four different losses. The original priority strip claimed a fixed intervention order. Use condition-specific protection.

title: Layer groundsheets without funneling rainwater under the tent floor
observation: Protruding groundsheet and runoff arrows are clearer than the predecessor cutaway. A fixed offset is unnecessary and can conflict with the shelter model.

title: Stack foam and inflatable pads for cold ground insulation
observation: Physical stack separates bag loft, inflatable and foam on the substrate. Layers are readable and support the puncture fallback without a stated system rating.

title: Compare A-frame, lean-to and low-storm tarp pitch configurations
observation: Three presentable tarp profiles make side orientation and storm-height tradeoffs apparent. Treat profiles as concepts and retain anchoring and local weather limits.

title: Match stakes and anchors to soil, sand, mud and compacted snow limits
observation: Angle and pull direction add value, but only two substrates are drawn and there is no wet-mud failure-state section. Do not turn the profiles into rated anchor instructions. Shelter reviewer to validate soil-specific detail.
specialist: Shelter equipment and geotechnical field safety

title: Prevent drifting snow from sealing shelter exits and high vents overnight
observation: Snow lip visibly obstructs the opening. The single vent and tools could suggest this is adequate. Added an instability and repeated-blockage boundary.

title: Keep fuel stoves, lanterns and heaters completely outside tents and vestibules
observation: Tent and outdoor cases are recognizable. Open sky alone does not establish a safe location. Show separation from shelter and openings.
specialist: Carbon monoxide safety and fire prevention

title: Balance heat, fuel and oxygen in a controlled small fire
observation: Visible fuel, flame and air paths explain the fire triangle better than the predecessor boxes. Consider local rules and fire-scale limits before field use.

title: Separate dry deadwood interior from wet or rotted bark
observation: Growth-ring section visualizes wet outer material and dry interior. The heading implied standing wood collection while the card specifies downed wood.

title: Stage fuel lay geometry for steady airflow without smothering
observation: Open tinder and constricted log stack communicate airflow contrast. Do not interpret the drawing as proof a particular lay is safe in local conditions.

title: Understand ferrocerium rod scraping mechanics and spark direction
observation: Striker contact and rod motion are apparent. A numeric angle conflicts with the implement description and is not necessary to communicate motion.

title: Trace friction-ember dust formation and notch geometry in wood drills
observation: The exploded view is closer to physical objects, but the cord-driving relationship and ember transfer are not depicted. Verify tool geometry and notch limits in a supervised demonstration before approval.

title: Refuel liquid stoves safely on cleared ground away from ignition
observation: The staged zones are clearer than prior boxes. A marked safe gap and generic depressurization read as manufacturer-independent steps. Remove those implications.
specialist: Portable appliance safety and fire prevention

title: Match stove windscreens, pot supports and fuel bottles to manufacturer specs
observation: The partial screen appears on the side labelled safe and the touch cue implies clearance. Changed to model-specific instructions and removed touch testing from text.

title: Enforce zero indoor charcoal, stove or unvented heater rules
observation: House section and separate action block place evacuation before equipment handling. The simple iconography supports the intended immediate decision.
specialist: Carbon monoxide safety and emergency medicine

title: Separate visual clarity from biological and chemical safety
observation: Three sample forms separate clarity, germs and chemical hazards. The appearance comparison usefully shows why clear water cannot establish safety.

title: Assess moving streams versus stagnant ponds and pools
observation: Two water bodies show different sediment and surface cues. Removed the universal collection cue in favor of watershed and contamination screening.

title: Collect from shallow streams without disturbing bottom sediment
observation: Water-flow and scoop orientation show sediment avoidance versus disturbing the bed. Retain the stable-footing prerequisite in the card.

title: Melt snow safely without scorching vessels or wasting fuel
observation: Water layer and snow positions are visible. Replaced unsupported air-gap/scorch wording with a bounded dry-heating warning.
specialist: Cold-weather operations and portable appliance safety

title: Pre-filter coarse particles with cloth or coffee filter before treatment
observation: Cloth funnel and receiving container show the coarse particle step. The lower label clearly separates this step from microbial treatment.

title: Understand what pore-size filtration removes and what passes through
observation: Rejected the combined virus/chemical outlet and categorical pore assurance. Rebuilt as two decision paths with exact model verification and alternate-source language.

title: Operate pump, squeeze and gravity filters without cross-contaminating outlets
observation: Raw side, flow arrow and clean receiver give a useful handling boundary. Device-specific interfaces remain within manufacturer instructions.

title: Recognize why boiling and chlorine fail against algal and chemical toxins
observation: Heat and vapor path improves on category boxes but pure steam and an absolute concentration claim imply unsupported chemistry. Plate and text delimited.

title: Iron Formations, Hematite, Magnetite and Compass Deflection
observation: Compass icons establish the kind of interference. The silhouette cannot establish magnetite or a predictable bearing deflection, and requires geological example and scope review.

title: Understand wood grain, knots and decay before shaping deadfall
observation: Grain, knot and decay become recognizable material states. Use reject cues for observation and avoid treating grain appearance as a load rating.
specialist: Forestry tool safety and wood mechanics

title: Understand steel edge geometry, toughness and brittleness
observation: Distinct edge silhouettes show slicing, chopping and a damage cue. Conceptual section does not specify a universal grind or toughness rating.

title: Tie and verify a bowline for a non-slip fixed utility loop
observation: Drawn cord crossing and terminal dot do not establish a dressed bowline. Unsafe sketch withdrawn and a reconstruction hold substituted.

title: Tie a figure-eight loop and stopper knot for secure termination
observation: The weave is a two-color zigzag and merges a stopper with a loop. Unsafe sketch withdrawn pending independently checked topology in two views.

title: Recognize spring poles and hung-up deadfall before making a cut
observation: Stored-energy and pinned-wood relationships improve on boxes. The single recoil arc cannot establish a safe path. Keep avoidance instructions and have qualified reviewer check the hazard envelope.
specialist: Forestry safety and wildland trail maintenance

title: Use an axe or hatchet only on a low stable chopping block
observation: Block and axe are recognizable, but the circle labelled Kneel does not depict body and hand placement or actual swing clearance. Require a qualified tool instructor and revised posture view.

title: Use first-class levers and stable fulcrums to shift heavy downed logs
observation: Effort and lift arrows distinguish lever arms. The drawn contact is oversimplified and lacks rolling/crush exclusion geometry. Require verified contact and equipment limits.
specialist: Mechanical safety and forestry tool safety

title: Spot suspected internal bleeding and prioritize urgent EMS evacuation
observation: Torso regions aid recognition, but keep flat was unconditional. Removed it and aligned positioning language to dispatch and suspected injury.

title: Prevent and protect friction blisters and foot-skin breakdown
observation: Pad bears outside the blister dome but air-gap geometry and infection claim overstate dressing protection. Clinician to verify pressure distribution and care limits.

title: Maintain spinal motion restriction after high-force falls or impacts
observation: The horizontal surrogate implied forced neutral alignment. Labels now preserve position found and airway or scene exceptions. Clinical sign-off remains open.

title: Shield blunt or penetrating eye trauma without applying pressure
observation: Shield arch conveys non-contact geometry. Removed the unsupported both-eyes cover cue and separated mechanical injury from chemical exposure.

title: Stabilize cold-water immersion survivors and guard against post-rescue collapse
observation: Wrap layers are apparent, but the unconditional horizontal directive conflicts with dispatch and airway priorities. Revised figure and text.

title: Distinguish early frostnip from superficial and deep frostbite
observation: Colored blocks imply visible grading certainty. Changed to appearance limitations and retained protection from refreezing. No clinical diagnostic approval.

title: Wash urushiol oils promptly and avoid deadly poison-ivy smoke inhalation
observation: Skin-contact and smoke panels separate exposure routes. Image avoids identification or treatment timing claims and retains the emergency boundary.

title: Protect personal prescription medications from cold, heat, and loss
observation: Protected carry is useful, but a fixed outside-pack threshold appeared to cover all products. Now require product-specific storage limits.
specialist: Pharmacy safety, wilderness medicine, and accessible preparedness

title: Take a field-to-map bearing and verify with a reciprocal back-bearing
observation: The actual line was approximately 78 degrees despite the 060 label. Rebuilt true screen geometry with the exact reciprocal and common reference.

title: Follow a compass bearing in forest using short visible leapfrog targets
observation: Consecutive targets make the route concept legible. Direction is fixed along the drawn leg and the card keeps the footing and visibility conditions.

title: Box cleanly around a pond, cliff or blowdown using right-angle offsets
observation: The four legs visibly preserve perpendicular offsets and approximate return line. Keep route safety and measured pace uncertainty in the chapter.

title: Cross-check two visible landmark bearings for an approximate position fix
observation: Two bearings demonstrate uncertainty better than boxes. Removed the unneeded angle range and corrected the three-landmark caption mismatch.

title: Read cloud sequences signaling an approaching warm or cold front
observation: Front profiles distinguish relative slopes. Added conditional weather wording to avoid implying deterministic precipitation or lightning.

title: Use VHF/FRS/GMRS short-range radios within realistic terrain line-of-sight limits
observation: Clear path and terrain shadow are legible. Relay position must be conditional on terrain and weather. Removed automatic climb direction.

title: Deploy high-contrast ground markers and mirror flashes for air or ground search
observation: Mirrored ray and ground marker add physical content, but mirror aiming and aircraft handling need an SAR reviewer and approved signal guidance.
specialist: Search and rescue and aviation safety

title: Orient a paper map to terrain using a baseplate compass
observation: Compass and meridian shown separated and the diagram does not show the two instruments’ relationship or which corrections are applied. Redraw with a verified compass and explicit north reference. The prior figure is withdrawn in the reader.

title: Distinguish clear solid new ice, white snow-ice and rotten honeycomb ice
observation: Ice structures have useful visual differences, but captions can be read as strength or crossing clearance. Removed the numerical comparison and emphasized observation limits.

title: Recognize how snow blankets insulate thin ice and hide open holes
observation: Snow bridge and hidden opening are visible. Corrected apparent safe bare ice and removed instructions to enter and sample from an observation-only page.

title: Execute cold-water ice self-rescue boundaries when falling through alone
observation: Body and entry direction illustrate conceptual self-exit. Removed fixed one-minute delay and guarantee of entry-side strength. Maintain rescue review.
specialist: Ice rescue specialist, EMS and wilderness medicine

title: Use HELP and group HUDDLE postures in cold water while wearing flotation
observation: The orange blocks omit fitted flotation and body/airway geometry. Withdraw the posture drawing pending an authentic staged and instructor-validated reference.

title: Consolidate household heat into one safe insulated interior room
observation: Room-within-room is readable. Changed door-blocking language to preserving escape routes and retained warming-center and combustion limits.
specialist: Cold-weather emergency management and residential safety

title: Maintain wood stoves and chimneys safely to prevent creosote flue fires
observation: Stove and flue are recognizable but fixed 36-inch spacing conflicts with appliance-specific listing. Removed the generic figure and manuscript requirement.
specialist: Certified chimney sweep, fire service, and HVAC safety

title: Prevent frozen residential plumbing pipes during sub-zero cold snaps
observation: Wall and pipe spacing clarify an exposure path. Qualified plumber to verify applicability before the illustrated airflow could be read as a universal thawing treatment.
specialist: Licensed plumber and cold-weather residential safety

title: Operate the main residential water shutoff valve to limit burst-pipe flooding
observation: Lever states are differentiated; handed wheel closure can depend on equipment. Require verification of direction and stop at a stuck or suspect valve.

title: Build barrier-lined raised beds for urban lead, clay, or wet soils
observation: Soil section looks like complete contaminant isolation and labeled a universal 12 inches. Replaced with EPA test-based limits for crop, bed and dust controls.

title: Separate low-acid foods (pressure canner ONLY) from high-acid foods
observation: Separate methods are useful, but fixed temperatures and a pH wall could be read as a complete process. Use tested recipe, equipment and altitude decisions.
specialist: Food microbiology and preservation process authority

title: Inspect Mason canning jars, sealing rims, and single-use two-piece lids
observation: Exploded closure and rim are identifiable. Headspace is recipe-specific and needs no generic numeric range in the visual.

title: Store home-canned jars cool, dark, dry, and unstacked for quality and safety
observation: Visible ring-free jars show storage arrangement. Removed the promise that failed seals will be immediately obvious.
specialist: Food preservation and food storage specialist

title: Shelter safely inside a stranded winter vehicle and guard against exhaust CO
observation: Exhaust arrow and tailpipe are visible. Vehicle-specific ventilation and engine timing need emergency and CO review. Do not infer window position assures safety.
specialist: Winter emergency response and carbon monoxide safety

title: Move immediately to lowest interior tornado shelter on Tornado Warnings
observation: Low interior location is well differentiated from exterior openings. Keep official warning and building-specific shelter conditions visible in text.
specialist: Meteorology, structural safety, and emergency management

title: Seek safe elevated refuge if sudden flash floodwater traps roads or homes
observation: The road washout figure was for the adjacent flood card. Rebuilt actual building elevation and closed attic versus necessary roof refuge.

title: Avoid hidden biological, chemical, and electrical hazards in floodwater
observation: Panel, debris and waterline convey otherwise invisible mixed hazards. The illustration prohibits contact with the panel and supports the isolation decision.

title: Pack by failure mode
observation: Pack and groups show functional staging, albeit stylized. The accompanying retrieve-and-test cue makes it useful at editorial level.
specialist: Field education and search and rescue

title: Leave a drainage channel early
observation: The original upward arrow began adjacent to the flood channel and the label crossed the ground line. Separated the dry route and removed the overlap.

title: Cleavage Planes vs Conchoidal and Hackly Fracture
observation: Cleavage and conchoidal profiles communicate two distinct breaks, but the third named hackly profile is missing. Add a verified third view after geologist review.

title: Understand the force on a fixed pulley redirect
observation: Vector direction and ideal magnitudes are useful. Clarified they depict rope load and the opposing support reaction, not a rating.

title: Apply commercial tourniquet limits and EMS time documentation
observation: The simulated wound and directional figure match the intended relationship. The band lacks device anatomy and the placement must be verified by a qualified instructor.

title: Reconcile true, grid and magnetic north before converting bearings
observation: True, grid and magnetic arrows are distinguishable. The page retains map legend, current location and reference-sign checks.

title: Position portable generators strictly outdoors at least 20 feet from buildings
observation: Distance from the building and outward exhaust direction are visually distinct. The card retains fully outdoor placement and nearby openings caveats.
specialist: Carbon monoxide safety, fire service, and licensed electrician

title: Operate a pressure canner cleanly: 10-minute steam vent and target PSI
observation: Vent path is visible. The old depiction left jar bases entirely above water and hid rack support. Clarified loaded waterline and added rack legs.
specialist: Food preservation process authority and Extension

title: Shelter-in-place properly for chemical or hazardous-materials airborne plumes
observation: Two hazards use explicit independent boundaries and the exit arrow for internal exposure. The external plume remains conditional on official direction.
